title: Slice out the middle item(s)
description:
Slice out the middle item or items from the food_stuff_tp tuple or food_stuff_lt list.

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as middle_items(food_stuff), where food_stuff is a tuple or list, returning the middle item as a one-item slice when the length is odd, or the two middle items as a two-item slice when the length is even (the return type must match the input type: slicing a tuple yields a tuple, slicing a list yields a list).
hints: The middle depends on whether the sequence has an odd or even number of items - an odd length has one true middle item, an even length has two.
Slicing (unlike indexing a single position) naturally returns the same type as the sequence you sliced, whether that's a tuple or a list, which is exactly what's needed here.
Use mid = len(food_stuff) // 2, then return food_stuff[mid:mid+1] if the length is odd, else food_stuff[mid-1:mid+1].
expected_behavior: Returns a slice containing the single middle item for odd-length input, or the two middle items for even-length input, matching the input's type.
explanation: Integer floor division gives the midpoint index; for an odd length that index alone is the true middle, so a one-item slice around it is taken, while for an even length there are two middle items straddling the midpoint, captured with a two-item slice.
